site.name: harness info
site.description: A step-by-step guide to running Claude Code unattended: what a harness is, the roles, how a coordinator delegates, the loop's contracts, and how to start, pause and stop it.

home.title: A harness runs Claude Code unattended
home.lead: A harness is a small program around Claude Code. It gives the agent one unit of work at a time, checks the result with code instead of taking the agent's word, and keeps all its state in files. A run can go for hours, and you can pause it at any moment.
home.flowLead: You write a two-line draft. Agents turn it into a spec, a plan, code, a review and a commit. You step in only where a human decision is needed.
home.readLead: Ten pages, about fifty-five minutes. Each one has a single goal, stated at the top.
home.goal: Understand what a harness is and pick where to start.

flow.label: One task moving across the board

logic.draft: You create T-002, "Do not add the same URL twice", with a title and two lines of draft, then press Submit.
logic.spec: The spec unit starts. The writer turns the draft into a spec and finds nothing to ask, so the harness moves the card on.
logic.plan: The plan unit: the explorer maps the code and the existing tests, then the planner writes the phases, the scope, the gate and one [closes] criterion.
logic.planned: The plan waits for you. You approve it, and because this is a logic task, it skips the prototype.
logic.ready: Approved and waiting. The next unit picks it up.
logic.implementing: The implement unit: the harness creates the branch harness/T-002-…, the tester writes the test and the implementer the code. The gate is green, so the harness commits.
logic.qa: The qa unit runs every [closes] command and the gate, checks the criteria it can, and prints qa: PASS.
logic.judge: The judge unit, a different model, re-runs the [closes] command and looks for a reason to reject. It prints judge: CONFIRMED.
logic.done: Confirmed. Without PR delivery, the commit on the task branch is the delivery, and the card stays here.
logic.delivered: With deliver.pr: true, the runner pushes the branch and opens a pull request itself: no agent, no tokens. A human merges it.

ui.draft: You create T-001 with kind ui: a search box that filters the bookmark list.
ui.spec: The writer starts the spec and hits a product decision it should not guess.
ui.ask: It writes Q1 with three options, the recommended one first, and ends the unit. The card waits for you.
ui.answer: You pick an option on the card. No question is open any more, so the harness sends the task back to spec.
ui.plan: The spec is finished. The explorer maps the list component, and the planner writes the plan with the prototype route in its scope.
ui.planned: You approve the plan. A ui task goes to the prototype step first.
ui.drafting: The designer builds a clickable prototype and takes a screenshot. The card shows drafting.
ui.comment: The prototype is in review. You leave a comment, and the designer goes another round.
ui.accept: The second round looks right. You press Accept.
ui.ready: Approved and waiting for the implement unit.
ui.implementing: The tester writes the test for the filter and the implementer the code. The gate is green: one commit.
ui.qa: qa types into the search box, checks the list and an empty search, and prints qa: PASS.
ui.judge: The judge re-runs the closing checks and prints judge: CONFIRMED.
ui.done: Done. The prototype route is dropped at delivery unless the plan keeps it.

bounce.ready: T-002 is approved with bounces: 0 in its frontmatter. The cap, limits.bounces, is 2.
bounce.round1: Round 1: the tester and the implementer ship the change, and the harness commits it.
bounce.qaFail: qa finds a criterion that fails and prints qa: FAIL. The task goes back, and bounces becomes 1.
bounce.round2: Round 2 starts with the debugger: it reads the qa report and hands the implementer a diagnosis. A second commit.
bounce.rejected: The judge rejects the work. That rejection brings bounces to 2, which is the cap.
bounce.parked: So the task is not sent back again. It is parked for a human, with the reason in its frontmatter.
bounce.reopen: You read the reason and press Reopen once the cause is dealt with. bounces goes back to 0, and the task returns to implementing.

sequence.label: One unit as a sequence of messages

implement.prepare: The runner picks T-002 in implementing, switches to its branch and takes a snapshot of the tree.
implement.start: It starts the coordinator: claude -p with the implement prompt, the standing rules and ## This run.
implement.tester: The coordinator calls the tester first: write the test for the [closes] criterion, in the project's own stack.
implement.testerDone: The tester reports back with the new test.
implement.implementer: Then the implementer: make the test pass, inside the scope.
implement.hold: The call is asynchronous, so the coordinator holds the turn. It keeps making tool calls, reading the trace and the task file, instead of writing a final message.
implement.finish: Only now does the coordinator write its final message and exit.
implement.contracts: The runner checks the unit: scope, task file, gate. The implement stage needs no verdict line.
implement.commit: Everything is green. The runner commits the tests and the code together and moves the task to qa.

hold.prepare: The runner picks T-002 in qa and takes a snapshot.
hold.start: It starts a fresh coordinator with the qa prompt.
hold.dispatch: The coordinator calls qa: run every [closes] command and the gate, and check the criteria it can.
hold.hold: It holds the turn with tool calls while qa works.
hold.report: qa reports that every criterion is met.
hold.finish: The coordinator prints the line qa: PASS and exits.
hold.contracts: The runner checks scope (only .harness/artifacts/ was written), the task file and the trace. The qa: line is there.

early.prepare: The runner picks T-002 in qa and takes a snapshot.
early.start: It starts a fresh coordinator with the qa prompt.
early.dispatch: The coordinator calls qa: run every [closes] command and the gate, and check the criteria it can.
early.early: The coordinator writes “Waiting for the results”. A message without a tool call ends the turn, and claude -p exits.
early.lost: qa's answer has nobody left to receive it.
early.trace: The runner finds no qa: line in the unit's output. The trace contract fails: a hard stop, exit code 1.
early.park: The unit's changes go into the stash “harness quarantine: T-002 unit N”, the tree is restored, and the task is parked with the reason.

loop.label: The loop: supervisor, runner, coordinator, specialists and contracts

normal.lock: harness run starts the supervisor. It takes the lock .harness/trace/supervisor.lock, so a second loop on this checkout refuses to start.
normal.pick: The runner starts unit 1. It picks T-002 in spec, records it in running.json, and writes the stage's specialists to unit-0001.agents.json.
normal.work: The coordinator and the writer work in a fresh claude -p. Every output line goes to unit-0001.jsonl.
normal.check: The coordinator exits. The runner checks the contracts, moves T-002 to plan, appends a handoff, and exits with code 0.
normal.next: Unit 2 picks the same task in plan. One unit moves a task one step, and every step gets a fresh context.
normal.idle: Nothing is left to take, so the runner exits with code 3. The supervisor checks for new work every 30 seconds. With --once-through it would end the run here.

pause.run: Unit 4 is working on T-003 in implement.
pause.write: You run harness pause. It writes .harness/trace/PAUSE. The unit in flight does not notice and keeps working.
pause.finish: The unit finishes, its contracts run, and the runner exits with code 0.
pause.wait: At the unit boundary the supervisor finds PAUSE and waits, checking the file every 2 seconds. Nothing is in flight: a safe moment to edit and commit.
pause.resume: harness resume deletes PAUSE, and the next unit starts.

hardstop.run: Unit 7: the implementer works on T-004.
hardstop.stray: It also edits a file outside the task's scope.
hardstop.scope: The scope contract compares the tree with the snapshot and finds the stray file. A hard stop: exit code 1.
hardstop.stash: The runner moves the unit's changes into the stash harness quarantine: T-004 unit 7, restores the tree, and parks T-004 with the reason.
hardstop.next: The supervisor goes on with the next unit, on a clean tree.

usage.refused: The agent is refused because the usage limit is reached. The runner puts the tree back and exits with code 4. T-005 is untouched.
usage.probe: The supervisor waits. It probes the network every 30 seconds; the network is fine, so it naps for 30 minutes. After six hours of this it would give up and exit with code 4.
usage.retry: It tries again with the same task. This time the agent runs, and the unit ends with code 0.

stop.run: Unit 11 is working on T-006 in qa.
stop.write: You run harness stop. It writes .harness/trace/STOP. The unit keeps going.
stop.finish: The unit finishes, and its contracts run.
stop.exit: At the boundary the supervisor finds STOP, exits with code 0 and removes its lock. STOP stays until the next run starts and clears it.

states.label: The task state machine
states.legendHuman: a human move (the dashboard and the CLI offer only these)
states.legendAgent: a move the harness makes after a unit, in the colour of the stage's role
states.legendPark: park: a hard stop, from any unfinished status
states.reopen: the status it was parked from, by you
states.park: on a hard stop: scope, task file, trace, gate, an agent error or a timeout

guards.drafting: when the designer finishes a round
guards.review: while the prototype is in review

what.draft: You write the title and a few lines. Nothing runs until you submit it.
what.spec: The spec unit: the writer turns the draft into a spec, or asks a product question.
what.needs-input: Waiting for your answers. The harness returns the task to the stage in resume once no question is open.
what.plan: The plan unit: the explorer maps the code, the planner writes phases, scope, gate and criteria, or asks.
what.planned: The plan waits for your approval. Full autonomy skips this gate.
what.prototype: The designer drafts a prototype; then it waits in review for your Accept or Comment.
what.ready: Approved and waiting for the implement unit.
what.implementing: The implement unit: the tester and the implementer, with the debugger first after a bounce. The harness commits after a green gate.
what.qa: The qa unit runs every [closes] command and the gate, and checks the criteria it can. Read-only.
what.judge: The judge unit, a different model, re-runs every [closes] and tries to reject.
what.done: Confirmed. With deliver.pr on, the runner's delivery step comes next.
what.delivered: The branch is pushed and the pull request is open. A human merges it.
what.parked: Stopped with a reason in the frontmatter. Only you can reopen it.

projects.caption: Projects: every repository the harness knows.

markers.cli: The terminal does the same: harness projects add and harness example.
markers.row: One project: its tasks, how many of them wait for you, and the unit in flight (T-001 in qa).
markers.open: Open board goes to the project's board. Remove asks you to confirm.
markers.add: Add a project takes any local git repository. The loop creates .harness/ in it and touches nothing else until you submit a task.

board.alt: The board of the bookmarks project during a qa unit, with the Live dock on the right.
board.caption: The board while the loop runs: a qa unit checks T-001.

markers.waiting: The header counts the tasks that wait for you and says why each one waits.
markers.groups: Thirteen columns in five groups: Define, Plan, Build, Review, Finish. An empty column folds into a narrow rail.
markers.action: A card shows its stage track. When the card waits for you, it shows one action: Submit, Answer, Approve, Review or Reopen.
markers.running: The spinner marks the card a unit works on right now. At most one card has it.
markers.parked: A card in parked names the contract that stopped it: here a file, README.md, changed outside the task's scope.
markers.dock: The Live dock: the supervisor with Pause and Stop, the unit in flight, what comes next and the recent units.

task-questions.alt: The task drawer of T-003 with the writer's two questions and their lettered options.
task-questions.caption: A task in needs-input: the writer asks two questions.

markers.card: The task you opened stays outlined on the board.
markers.asker: Who asked and when: the writer, in the spec stage, in unit 5.
markers.tabs: The task file in tabs. Interview appears only when the task has questions.
markers.options: Each question has lettered options. The recommended one comes first, with its reason.
markers.note: An optional note for the agent goes with each answer.
markers.send: One button writes all the answers into the task file.
markers.draft: Your own draft stays at the bottom of the drawer.

prototype-review.alt: The task drawer of T-001 on the Prototype tab, with Accept, a comment box and the round's picture.
prototype-review.caption: A UI task in prototype: round 1 waits for your review.

markers.card: T-001 is a UI task, so it stops in Prototype before it is built. The card shows the round and asks you to Review.
markers.tab: The Prototype tab appears for UI tasks.
markers.comment: Or write what the next round should change. The drawer shows how many rounds are left.
markers.preview: The round's picture from the task's artifacts folder. Units have no browser, so the designer usually draws prototype.svg, a 1440 px wireframe with the page's real copy, layout and colours; prototype.png appears when an allowed command can take a screenshot. Here the fake agent drew it.
markers.draft: Your draft, to compare the picture with what you asked for.

live.alt: The Live trace screen: the unit list, the running qa unit with its agents, and the supervisor log.
live.caption: Live trace during unit 12. Durations are real; the costs are demo numbers.

markers.units: Every unit the loop ran, newest first. The top one runs now.
markers.hardstop: Unit 8 ended in a hard stop, and T-004 went to parked.
markers.header: The unit in flight: its task, its stage, how long it has run and the specialists it may call.
markers.coordinator: The coordinator's lane: it handed the work to qa.
markers.specialist: The specialist's lane: each tool call with its time and the file name. Tool arguments and messages are never shown.
markers.log: The supervisor's log, newest first: starts, exit codes, status moves and commits.

stats.alt: The Stats screen: totals, costs per stage and per task, verdicts and permission denials.
stats.caption: Stats after the walkthrough. The tokens and costs are made up by the fake agent.

markers.tiles: Totals: units, API-equivalent cost, tokens, agent time and denied tool calls. Cost is the price claude -p reports; a subscription login is not billed per token.
markers.unknown: A unit whose agent printed no usage counts as unknown, not as zero.
markers.stage: Per stage, with its coordinator, the parked count and a bar for cost.
markers.task: Per task, with its current status.
markers.verdicts: The verdicts the coordinators printed: qa PASS, judge CONFIRMED.
markers.denials: Tool calls the permission mode refused. Frequent ones point to a missing entry in agent.allowedTools.

agents.alt: The Agents screen: the stage coordinators, the specialist matrix, the checks and the invocation.
agents.caption: Agents: who works each stage and how a unit starts Claude Code.

markers.coordinators: One coordinator per stage, each one claude -p on its model. The judge runs on opus.
markers.matrix: The specialists each unit gets through --agents. A dot marks the stage that offers one.
markers.pill: The checks that refuse a run, summed up.
markers.checks: The checks: the judge's model differs from the implementer's and the tester's, and every agent carries the current standing rules.
markers.invocation: How a unit starts Claude Code. This orange card appears only because AGENT_CMD points at the fake agent; a real project shows the plain claude command. With a real claude, a Billing row also says how the run is billed.
markers.integrations: Delivery and Telegram, both off here. Delivery needs deliver.pr; Telegram needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID.
markers.tools: Permission mode, setting sources and allowed tools. Commits and pushes are absent on purpose: the loop commits only after the contracts pass.

delivered.alt: The board with T-001 delivered and T-002 done, and the drawer of T-001 with its pull request link.
delivered.caption: Delivery by pull request: T-001 is delivered, T-002 is next.

markers.next: T-002 is done. With deliver.pr on, the card says PR next, and the grey spinner shows the loop takes it next.
markers.card: T-001 is delivered. The card links to its pull request, PR #1.
markers.link: The drawer says it again: Pull request #1, merging is yours. This URL comes from the fake gh, not from a real repository.
markers.track: The stage track is lit to the end: delivered is the last status.
